name: small broken concrete chunks with a rebar stub lying on the ground

surfaces.part: concrete chunk cluster (flat rubble pile on ground)

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a roughly 16x16 irregular patch (widths 11-16 over rows 1-14). It is seen from above as gray concrete fragments in light/mid-gray bands, with a dark rusty-brown rebar stub at rows 2-5. There is no front-edge line, no eave shadow, and no vertical south face of 3 or more rows. The only darker rows are outline rows at 14-15. The pile lies flat on the ground like a floor decal, so it reads as a flat top-down plate, which suits the kind 'flat'.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small prop that is under one tile in size, so I judged it by eye against the paving reference. It has about 5 grey steps, from a light top edge through mid greys to a dark underside, plus a reddish-brown rebar stub. Its dark edge pixels carry a tint (0% near-neutral), unlike the paving reference at 80% neutral, so the outline reads as a dark material tone and not a black sticker line. Measured facts are 13 visible tones per tile, above the grass reference at 3 and the paving reference at 7, and 0% near-flat coverage. No area is a flat fill. Texture is modest because the piece is tiny, but the chunk faces are broken into separate shaded facets. A careful artist would accept it next to the paving reference without it looking thinner or flatter.
